name: raw_not_empty
why: A failed or empty download must stop the pipeline, not publish an empty mart.
sql: SELECT CASE WHEN count(*) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM raw.sales WHERE snapshot_id = '{{snapshot_id}}'

name: raw_not_truncated
why: Sales history only grows. A snapshot with >10% fewer rows than the previous one is almost certainly a truncated export.
sql: SELECT CASE WHEN prev IS NOT NULL AND cur < 0.9 * prev THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM (SELECT (SELECT row_count FROM raw.ingestion_log WHERE snapshot_id = '{{snapshot_id}}') AS cur, (SELECT row_count FROM raw.ingestion_log WHERE snapshot_id <> '{{snapshot_id}}' ORDER BY loaded_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS prev)

name: sale_date_parsed
why: Dataset-specific: the data dictionary documents dd/mm/yyyy, but the export uses ISO dates. Any value that matches neither silently becomes NULL, so this fails if the format drifts.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM staging.stg_sales WHERE sale_date_raw IS NOT NULL AND sale_date IS NULL

name: parcel_id_present
why: A sale without a parcel cannot be attributed to a property or municipality.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM staging.stg_sales WHERE parcel_id IS NULL OR parcel_id = ''

name: parcel_id_format
why: The dictionary says PARID is 16 characters. Other lengths suggest truncation or a different ID scheme.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM staging.stg_sales WHERE length(parcel_id) <> 16

name: price_not_negative
why: A negative consideration is never valid.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM staging.stg_sales WHERE price < 0

name: sale_date_not_in_future
why: Sales cannot occur after the data was published.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM staging.stg_sales WHERE sale_date > current_date

name: recorded_before_sale
why: Deeds are recorded after the sale. Recording more than 30 days earlier points to a data entry error.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM staging.stg_sales WHERE record_date < sale_date - INTERVAL 30 DAY

name: sale_id_unique
why: The fact table grain is one row per parcel sale. Duplicates would double count.
sql: SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT sale_id) FROM fact.fct_sales

name: market_sales_have_real_price
why: Guards the market-sale rule: $0 and $1 transfers must never reach price statistics.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM fact.fct_sales WHERE is_market_sale AND (price IS NULL OR price < 1000)

name: multi_parcel_deeds_excluded
why: Dataset-specific: one deed can cover several parcels with the full price repeated on each row. No deed may contribute more than one market sale.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT deed_book, deed_page, sale_date FROM fact.fct_sales WHERE is_market_sale AND deed_book IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*) > 1)

name: multi_parcel_price_is_repeated
why: Dataset-specific: verifies the assumption above. If parcels on one deed carry different prices, the price may be split rather than repeated, and the exclusion rule should be revisited.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT deed_book, deed_page, sale_date FROM fact.fct_sales WHERE is_multi_parcel GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(DISTINCT price) > 1)

name: mart_grain_unique
why: The mart must have exactly one row per municipality per year.
sql: SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT (municipality_code, sale_year)) FROM mart.muni_year_market_sales

name: mart_quantiles_ordered
why: p25 <= median <= p75 must always hold; otherwise the aggregation is wrong.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM mart.muni_year_market_sales WHERE median_price IS NOT NULL AND NOT (p25_price <= median_price AND median_price <= p75_price)

name: mart_market_le_recorded
why: Market sales are a subset of recorded transfers.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM mart.muni_year_market_sales WHERE market_sales > recorded_transfers

name: dates_have_plausible_year
why: Dataset-specific: a record date with the year 212 parsed as a valid date, so the parse check missed it. Dates before 1900 are data entry errors. A small known number is tolerated; a jump means a systemic problem.
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM staging.stg_sales WHERE year(sale_date) < 1900 OR year(record_date) < 1900
